title: Birbal's Clever Counting of Crows
summary: When Emperor Akbar asks his court how many crows inhabit the royal capital of Agra, Birbal gives an ingenious answer that no one can disprove.
moral: Quick wit and graceful humor can turn an impossible challenge into a delightful victory.
full_text:
One crisp autumn morning, Emperor Akbar and his trusted advisor Birbal were walking through the royal pleasure gardens of Agra. The trees were filled with fluttering birds, and noisy black crows were cawing from every sandstone minaret.

Akbar turned to Birbal with a sly smile. 'Birbal, you claim to have an answer for every riddle under the sun. Tell me truthfully: exactly how many crows are there in our imperial capital of Agra?'

The courtiers held their breath, expecting Birbal to hesitate. Instead, Birbal smiled warmly and bowed. 'Your Majesty, there are exactly forty-two thousand, nine hundred and fifty-three crows in the city of Agra.'

Akbar looked astonished. 'How can you be so certain? What if my royal inspectors count more crows than that?'

'If there are more, Your Majesty,' replied Birbal without missing a beat, 'it simply means their relatives from neighboring kingdoms have come to visit them on holiday.'

'And what if there are fewer crows?' challenged the Emperor with a twinkle in his eye.

'Then, Sire, it means some of our Agra crows have flown away to visit their relatives in Delhi or Jaipur!'

Akbar burst into a hearty laugh, delighted by Birbal's dazzling presence of mind. Once again, wit had disarmed an impossible question with kindness and joy.
